newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut nabs 10 in food-stamp fraud haul.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut nabs 10 in food-stamp fraud haul.

text.p: Ten people were arrested in New England's biggest-ever crackdown on food-stamp fraud, Connecticut and federal officials said Tuesday.
The arrests in Hartford and New Britain climaxed an 18-month investigation, Connecticut Chief State's Attorney John M. Bailey told a news conference.
The probe, conducted with the U.S. Department of Agriculture, involved the allegedly improper use of more than $100,000 in food stamps, Bailey said.
Using food stamps, undercover investigators were able to purchase automobiles and weapons, among other items.
State officials have also issued an arrest warrant for Hartford state Representative Edwin Garcia in connection with the investigation.
Bailey did not comment on the specific charges against Garcia.
"The warrant has not been served yet. They are presently seeking him," a spokesman in Bailey's office told Reuters.
Bailey said it was likely that more arrests would follow, and that 14 warrants have been issued.
Of the 10 arrested, two also face federal charges.
All are charged with felonies and face substantial prison terms with a maximum of 20 years if convicted.
Most of the accused are being held on bonds ranging from $100,000 to $500,000 pending arraignment in Hartford Superior Court.
About $175 million in food stamps are issued in Connecticut each year. --Hartford newsroom (860) 727-0224
